text: EchoLens turns two NISAR radar passes into an incident briefing: what changed, how many square kilometres, and why we trust it. Smoke and cloud hide fires from cameras. L-band radar still sees.
Nine real incidents on one globe. Detected, negative, and marginal — including honest negatives where the radar correctly says nothing left.
Snyder Fire is the exam with an answer key. Same NISAR track, June seventeen before, July twenty-three after. Official NIFC perimeter in yellow.
This is not a photograph. Blue is darker after the fire — the scar. Our change sits inside the official line. Precision one point zero. Forty point nine square kilometres.
Before. After. Same look angle, same track. Then change — July minus June in decibels.
Same week in optical: Sentinel-two is thirty-four percent cloud. That is why we do not wait for a clear photo.
Coleman Creek is a grass fire. Almost invisible to L-band. Publishing no is part of the product.
EchoLens: two NISAR passes, one briefing. Built solo by Muhammad Umer Aamir. Live at echolens-theta.vercel.app.
